connections.name: Chat Connections
connections.description: Central address book of your groups and channels; target pickers across every module are powered from this list.

overview: Register each group, supergroup, and channel the bot operates in once — every target-chat field in the studio then offers them as a dropdown.
Chats the bot is added to are discovered automatically; Sync imports them with their titles and types.
Connections accept numeric ids (-100…) or public @usernames, and can be deactivated without deletion.
setup: Add the bot to the target group or channel as an administrator (posting rights are enough for channels).
Press Sync to import chats the bot already discovered, or add entries manually with their chat id or @username.
Reference the same list from the Scheduler, Support Desk, Giveaways, VIP Subscriptions, Paid Media, and Webhooks modules.
troubleshooting: A numeric chat id is required for private chats; @usernames only work for public channels and groups.
Sync only knows chats where the bot received at least one update (my_chat_member events).
Removing a connection never kicks the bot; it only removes the studio-side shortcut.

start-menu.name: Start Menu
start-menu.description: Unified /start menu: chat folder (addlist), channel, group, and web buttons with sections, layout control, click analytics, and /menu re-open.

overview: The consolidated start menu: every destination your bot offers on /start lives here — chat folder share links (t.me/addlist/...), channels, groups, and external web links.
Flat style renders one button list; categorized style groups destinations by type with section headers in the message text.
Button layout is controlled per row (1-4 columns) and users can re-open the menu anytime with /menu.
Click counters quantify engagement per menu item when tracking is enabled.
setup: In Telegram, create a chat folder and use its share link (t.me/addlist/...) as a menu item of type folder.
Add channels, groups, and web destinations as items of their matching type; order controls button position.
Set a start message with placeholders ({first_name}, {mention}) for a personalized header.
Optionally set a public base URL to route buttons through the built-in click tracker.
Send /start (or /menu) to the bot to verify the menu renders.
troubleshooting: Click tracking requires the studio to be reachable on a public HTTPS URL.
Telegram caches inline keyboards briefly; edits apply to newly sent menus.
When both this module and Custom Commands define a /start reply, the Start Menu takes priority.

menuStyle.label: Menu style
menuStyle.help: Flat shows one button list; categorized groups destinations with headers

enableMenuCommand.label: Enable /menu command
enableMenuCommand.help: Users can re-open the menu anytime with /menu

publicBaseUrl.label: Public base URL
publicBaseUrl.help: Required for click tracking, e.g. https://studio.example.com

scheduler.name: Channel Post Scheduler
scheduler.description: Timed channel posts with inline buttons and caption watermark.

overview: Queue posts to channels with precise dispatch times, rich media, and inline buttons.
A branded watermark line is appended to captions for consistent channel identity.
setup: Add the bot as an administrator in the target channel with permission to post.
Copy the channel id (@username or numeric) into the post form.
Schedule posts; the dispatcher checks every 30 seconds.
troubleshooting: Posts fail with 400 when the bot lacks admin rights in the target chat.
Times are stored and compared in UTC ISO format.

timezoneOffsetMinutes.label: Timezone offset (minutes, e.g. 180 for UTC+3)
timezoneOffsetMinutes.help: Local time offset for {date} and {time} placeholders and scheduling

targetChatId.label: Target chat
targetChatId.help: Pick a connected channel or group; manage the list in Chat Connections

support.name: Support Desk (Livegram)
support.description: Per-user forum topics in an admin supergroup with two-way relay.

overview: Every user message opens a dedicated forum topic in your admin supergroup.
Admins reply inside the topic; the bot relays the answer to the user.
Quick commands: /ban, /unban, /info while replying in a topic.
setup: Create a supergroup, enable Topics in its settings, and add the bot as an admin.
Copy the supergroup id into the configuration and save.
Users message the bot directly; topics appear automatically.
troubleshooting: Topic creation requires the bot to be an administrator with can_manage_topics.
The auto-reply is throttled per user to avoid spamming receipts.

adminChatId.label: Admin supergroup
adminChatId.help: Forum-enabled admin group; manage the list in Chat Connections

business.name: Business Secretary
business.description: Auto-answers clients writing to a Telegram Business account.

overview: Handles messages arriving through a manager personal Telegram Business connection.
Useful for after-hours acknowledgements and triage outside working time.
setup: In Telegram Business settings, connect the bot to the manager account.
Copy the emitted business_connection_id into the configuration.
Write a concise, professional auto-reply and enable the module.
troubleshooting: Business message APIs evolve; replies are sent through the raw Bot API surface.
If replies fail, verify the connection is still active in Telegram settings.

connectionId.label: Business connection id
connectionId.help: Leave empty to answer every connection

drip.name: Drip Sequences
drip.description: Timed multi-step sequences such as onboarding journeys.

overview: Classic day-1/day-3/day-7 onboarding and promotional journeys.
Each step delays a configurable number of minutes after the previous one.
Subscribers can be added manually or automatically on /start.
setup: Create a campaign with at least one step (delayMinutes + text).
Enable auto-subscribe on start or add subscribers from the campaign view.
The scheduler advances steps every 30 seconds.
troubleshooting: Users who blocked the bot are unsubscribed automatically on delivery failure.
delayMinutes counts from the previous step, not from subscription.

broadcast.name: Broadcast Engine
broadcast.description: Filtered mass messaging with 429-aware rate limiting.

overview: Send announcements to everyone, a language segment, or recently active users.
Rich media and inline buttons are supported with per-recipient placeholders.
Success and failure counters update live while the queue drains.
setup: Grow the audience first: every user who messages the bot is recorded.
Compose the broadcast, choose a target filter, and queue it.
Monitor progress in the history table.
troubleshooting: Telegram limits broadcasts to ~30 messages per second; the engine paces below that.
Users who blocked the bot count as failures and are skipped in spirit by future targeting.

crm.name: Audience CRM
crm.description: Subscriber profiles, tags, notes, and CSV/JSON export.

overview: Every bot interaction upserts a subscriber profile automatically.
Tag users into segments (VIP, beta, churn-risk) and keep internal notes.
Export the full audience as CSV or JSON for external tooling.
setup: No setup required; profiles accumulate as the bot runs.
Use tags as broadcast filters and segmentation hooks.
troubleshooting: Search matches username, name, and Telegram id.
Points shown here feed the referral and gamification modules.

welcome.name: Group Welcome & Goodbye
welcome.description: Media greetings with buttons, goodbyes, clean-welcome, and service cleanup.

mediaUrl.label: Welcome media URL
mediaUrl.help: Photo or video sent with the greeting caption

overview: Greets new members with templates, media and inline buttons.
Goodbye messages and clean-welcome keep exactly one greeting visible.
Join/leave service messages are removed automatically.
setup: Add the bot as a group administrator with delete permissions.
Compose templates with placeholders such as {mention} and {group_name}.
Attach a media URL and buttons JSON for rich greetings.
troubleshooting: Media greetings fall back to text when the URL cannot be sent.
Auto-delete accepts 15 seconds up to one hour.

captcha.name: Captcha Gatekeeper
captcha.description: Button, math or PM verification with kick timers and join requests.

mode.label: Mod
mode.help: pm-math challenges in PM and falls back to a button

joinRequestIntegration.label: Handle join requests via PM captcha

overview: Anti-raid gate: new members must verify within the configured window.
Button mode taps to verify; math replies with a sum; pm-math verifies in PM.
Members stay muted until verified and solve the captcha once per group.
setup: Add the bot as a group administrator with ban permissions.
Choose a mode and timeout, then enable the module.
troubleshooting: pm-math falls back to a group button when the user never started the bot.
Join-request integration needs chat_join_request updates (enabled).

moderation.name: Moderation & Anti-Spam
moderation.description: Blacklisted words, link blocking, flood control, strike escalation.

overview: Deletes messages matching blacklisted words (plain or /regex/ form), links, or floods.
Repeat offenders escalate to a studio-level ban and chat kick.
Banned users are listed here for review and manual unbans.
setup: Grant the bot administrator rights with message deletion.
Tune thresholds conservatively to avoid false positives.
troubleshooting: Regex entries use the /pattern/flags form, e.g. /\bfree crypto\b/i.
Flood windows are per user per group and held in memory.

blocklistMode.label: Blocklist mode
blocklistMode.help: Punishment for blocklist hits; per-entry {action} overrides this

blocklistDurationSeconds.label: Blocklist tban/tmute duration (seconds)
blocklistDurationSeconds.help: Duration for timed blocklist punishments (0 = default)

floodDurationSeconds.label: Flood punishment duration (seconds)
floodDurationSeconds.help: Duration for tmute/tban flood punishments (0 = default)

giveaways.name: Giveaways Engine
giveaways.description: Channel-gated giveaways with verifiable winner draws.

overview: Users join via /giveaway and inline Participate buttons.
Membership in required channels is verified through getChatMember.
Winners are drawn with a seeded shuffle reproducible from the participant list.
setup: Add the bot as an administrator in every required channel.
Create the giveaway with channel ids and an end time.
Announce /giveaway in your community to start collecting participants.
troubleshooting: Verification fails when the bot cannot see the channel member list.
Draws run every 60 seconds after ends_at passes.

requiredChannels.label: Required channels
requiredChannels.help: Membership gates verified on join; manage the list in Chat Connections

referrals.name: Referral Leaderboard
referrals.description: Deep-link referral tracking with point rewards and /top.

overview: Users share t.me/bot?start=ref_<id> deep links; attribution is automatic.
Referrers earn points instantly; /top shows the standing leaderboard.
setup: Enable the module and configure the reward per referral.
Broadcast the personal link pattern to your community.
troubleshooting: Self-referrals and repeat attributions are ignored.
The referrer must already be a known subscriber when the invitee arrives.

overview: sendPoll-powered quizzes with correct answers scored automatically.
Points and per-quiz scoreboards persist for leaderboards (/scoreboard).
setup: Create quizzes in the engagement tab (question, options, correct index, points).
Users start a random quiz with the configured command.
troubleshooting: Polls must be non-anonymous for scoring; the module enforces this.
Reactions analytics live in the same engagement tab.

reactions.name: Reaction Analytics
reactions.description: Tracks channel post reactions and rewards points.

overview: Counts emoji reactions on posts and awards points to the reacting member.
The summary chart shows which emojis resonate with the audience.
setup: Add the bot as an administrator in the tracked channel.
Reaction updates require the chat to permit bot reaction events.
troubleshooting: Anonymous reactor identities cannot be attributed and are skipped.
Emoji-only reactions are counted; paid and custom reactions are ignored.

message-score.name: Message Score & Leaderboard
message-score.description: Scores member activity in groups (messages, replies, media), lists the most active members, and posts rich leaderboards to one or many chats on a schedule.

overview: Every member message in your groups builds a per-day activity record: messages, replies to others, and media count separately.
The weighted score ranks the most active members for any period (today, 7 days, 30 days, or all time).
Rich leaderboard messages (header, per-member row template, footer, medals, parse mode, silent flag) can be sent instantly or on a recurring schedule to one or many connected chats.
Schedules support once, hourly, daily, and weekly recurrences in UTC.
setup: Disable bot privacy mode via BotFather (or make the bot an admin) so it can see member messages in groups.
Enable the module and tune the score weights in the configuration card.
Pick one or more target chats, design the message format with placeholders, and check the live preview.
Press Send now for a one-off posting, or Save as schedule to automate it.
troubleshooting: No members on the leaderboard usually means privacy mode is hiding group messages from the bot.
Service messages (joins, pins, title changes) never count towards the score.
Sending fails with 403 when the bot is not a member of the target chat or lacks posting rights.
Scheduled times use UTC; daily/weekly runs fire at the configured HH:mm.

messageWeight.label: Score per message
messageWeight.help: Weight added for every regular member message

replyWeight.label: Score per reply
replyWeight.help: Extra weight when a member replies to someone else

mediaWeight.label: Score per media message
mediaWeight.help: Weight for photos, videos, stickers, voice, and files

ai-assistant.name: AI Assistant
ai-assistant.description: 24/7 AI answering via OpenAI, Gemini, or any OpenAI-compatible URL (OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Ollama…).

overview: Answers private user messages around the clock with an enterprise tone.
Speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions protocol, so every OpenAI-compatible service works: OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Groq, Ollama, vLLM, and more; Gemini uses its native API.
Keeps a short per-user history for contextual answers.
setup: Pick a provider: openai, openrouter, gemini, or custom (your own OpenAI-compatible base URL).
Paste the API key, set the model id in the provider format (OpenRouter uses vendor/model such as openai/gpt-4o-mini), and tune the system prompt.
Use the built-in test button before enabling.
troubleshooting: The assistant defers to the support desk and autoresponder keyword rules.
Provider errors surface in the chat as a temporary-unavailable notice.
Voice transcription needs an OpenAI-compatible /audio/transcriptions endpoint; OpenRouter does not expose one, so set transcriptionModel against a compatible provider (OpenAI, Groq, local Whisper).

provider.label: Provider
provider.help: openrouter/custom call any model through the OpenAI-compatible base URL

baseUrl.label: Base URL (OpenAI-compatible)
baseUrl.help: Ignored for openai/openrouter. Custom example: http://localhost:11434/v1 (Ollama), https://api.deepseek.com/v1

model.label: Model
model.help: Provider model id: gpt-4o-mini, openai/gpt-4o-mini (OpenRouter), anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet (OpenRouter), gemini-2.0-flash

transcriptionModel.label: Voice transcription model
transcriptionModel.help: Model for voice notes on the OpenAI-compatible /audio/transcriptions endpoint; empty = whisper-1

smartHandoff.label: Smart human handoff (AI classifier)
smartHandoff.help: Classifies requests for a human agent with the LLM; falls back to keywords when off or on failure

showSources.label: Append knowledge sources to replies
showSources.help: Shows which knowledge base documents grounded the answer

embeddingModel.label: Embedding model (semantic RAG, optional)
embeddingModel.help: OpenAI-compatible embeddings, e.g. text-embedding-3-small; empty = keyword-only retrieval

knowledgeTags.label: Knowledge tag filter (optional)
knowledgeTags.help: Comma-separated tags; only docs carrying one of these are retrieved

autoresponder.name: Commands & Auto-Responder
autoresponder.description: Custom /commands and keyword triggers with media.

overview: Custom commands like /pricing and /faq answered instantly with media.
Non-slash triggers match message substrings as keyword auto-responders.
setup: Create rules; commands must start with /, keywords must not.
Photo URLs and inline buttons are optional enhancements.
troubleshooting: When the Start Menu module owns /start, its menu takes precedence.
Keyword rules also pause AI assistant replies to avoid double answers.

paid-media.name: Paid Media Paywall
paid-media.description: Stars-locked photos and videos via sendPaidMedia.

overview: Sends media that users unlock by paying Telegram Stars.
Funds settle to the bot owner's Fragment balance.
setup: Send paid media from the monetization tab to any chat id.
Price each send in Stars; recipients see a native paywall.
troubleshooting: Requires a Bot API version supporting sendPaidMedia.
Media must be publicly reachable URLs.

vip-subs.name: VIP Subscriptions
vip-subs.description: Star-priced channel invites with expiry enforcement.

overview: createChatSubscriptionInviteLink generates Star-billed invite links.
Expired members are removed automatically by the sweep timer.
setup: Create a private channel and add the bot as an administrator.
Set the channel id, period, and Star price, then grant subscriptions.
troubleshooting: The channel must allow the bot to manage invite links.
Removal uses ban + unban, so the member can rejoin after renewing.

channelChatId.label: VIP channel
channelChatId.help: Private channel the bot administrates; manage the list in Chat Connections

webhooks.name: Webhooks Hub
webhooks.description: Signed outgoing events and inbound automation triggers.

overview: Stream events (orders, form submissions, support activity) to Zapier, Make, or n8n.
Every delivery is signed with HMAC-SHA256 in X-Studio-Signature.
Inbound hooks render templated messages into a chat from external systems.
setup: Register an outgoing endpoint with a shared secret and event filter.
Verify signatures on the receiving side before trusting payloads.
For inbound, create a hook and POST JSON to its URL.
troubleshooting: Empty event lists subscribe an endpoint to every event.
Failed deliveries are logged in the delivery log tab.

mini-apps.name: Mini App Studio
mini-apps.description: Create, host, and publish Telegram Mini Apps without external hosting.

overview: Build and host Telegram Mini Apps directly from the studio on the unified /tma/* route.
Five enterprise templates: E-Commerce storefront, Loyalty hub, dynamic Forms, daily Spin wheel, and external Webview wrapper.
The embedded phone preview renders the live app; publishing wires the chat menu button in one click.
setup: Create a BotFather bot and register it in the studio (the bot must be running).
Create a Mini App, pick a template, and adjust its JSON configuration.
Host HTTPS is required by Telegram: set the public base URL before publishing.
Publish to set the chat bottom-left menu button via setChatMenuButton.
troubleshooting: Telegram requires an HTTPS public URL for Mini Apps; localhost only works inside Telegram Desktop with flags.
Mini App API calls are validated with initData HMAC-SHA256 signatures tied to the owning bot token.
The Webview template cannot frame sites that send X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors restrictions.

group-moderation.name: Group Moderation Commands
group-moderation.description: In-group admin commands: ban, mute, kick, warnings, purges, approvals, silent actions.

warnLimit.label: Warning limit
warnLimit.help: Warnings before the warn mode punishment fires (0 disables)

warnMode.label: Warning mode
warnMode.help: Punishment applied when the warn limit is reached

silentActions.label: Silent actions
silentActions.help: s-commands and punishments without confirmation messages

adminError.label: Reply to non-admins
adminError.help: Show "admin only" errors to unauthorized users

warnDurationSeconds.label: Warn mode duration (seconds)
warnDurationSeconds.help: Duration for tban/tmute warn modes (0 = default)

overview: Full admin command set directly in the group chat.
ban/mute/kick families with timed (tban/tmute), delete (d*) and silent (s*) variants.
Persistent warnings with configurable limit, mode and expiry, plus purge commands.
Approvals make trusted members immune to automated moderation.
setup: Enable the module, then use /ban, /mute, /warn, /purge and friends in the group.
The bot must be a group administrator with restrict and delete rights.
Tune defaults here; groups can override them with /setwarnlimit and /setwarnmode.
troubleshooting: Purges only reach messages younger than 48 hours (Telegram limitation).
Warnings persist in the database; /resetwarn clears a user entirely.

group-tools.name: Group Admin Tools
group-tools.description: Pins, user reports, admin list, /id and /info lookups, echo, and command disabling.

cleanLinked.label: Delete linked channel posts
cleanLinked.help: Removes forwarded channel messages from the discussion group

overview: Pin family: /pin, /pin loud, /permapin, /unpin, /unpinall, plus linked-channel controls.
User reports: /report and @admin tag every admin invisibly.
Lookups (/id, /info), admin listing, promote/demote, and /echo.
Per-group command disabling with /disable and /enable.
setup: Enable the module; every command checks native Telegram admin permissions.
Pin commands need the pin right; disabling commands needs change-info rights.
troubleshooting: Admins cannot be reported.
Anonymous admins are trusted with full non-owner rights.

locks.name: Chat Locks
locks.description: Fine-grained content locks: stickers, gifs, polls, forwards, links, scripts and more.

lockedTypes.label: Locked types (one per line)
lockedTypes.help: Run /locktypes in the group for the full list

overview: 45+ lock types: media kinds, stickers, polls, forwards, links, buttons.
Script locks (rtl, cjk, cyrillic, zalgo) and anonymous-channel protection.
Allowlist entries exempt specific domains, packs, forwards and commands.
Custom punishments per lock via /lock <types> ### reason {action}.
setup: Enable the module and lock content types with /lock gif poll url.
Admins and approved users are always exempt.
troubleshooting: Locks run before blocklists.
Bot senders and service messages are never locked.

antiraid.name: AntiRaid
antiraid.description: Temporarily bans joiners during raid attacks, manually or automatically.

overview: Raid mode bans every new joiner for a short period so raids drain out.
Manual /antiraid on/off or a custom duration.
/autoantiraid N enables automatically when N users join within a minute.
setup: Enable the module and arm raid mode with /antiraid on when under attack.
Tune durations so innocent late joiners are not banned for long.
troubleshooting: Raid state lives in memory; a restart disarms active raid mode.
CAPTCHAs or join requests prevent spam-joining entirely.

rules.name: Group Rules
rules.description: Per-group rules with /rules delivery and the {rules} placeholder button.

overview: /rules shows the group rules in chat or via a PM deep-link button.
The {rules} placeholder embeds the same link into welcome messages.
Manage with /setrules, /resetrules, /privaterules and /setrulesbutton.
setup: Enable the module and set the rules text (or use /setrules in the group).
Users must start the bot in PM for private rule delivery.
troubleshooting: Empty rules text makes /rules reply "no rules set".
The deep link only works with a public bot username.

admin-log.name: Admin Log Channel
admin-log.description: Forwards admin actions and automated punishments to a Telegram log channel.

logChatId.label: Log channel id
logChatId.help: Numeric channel id the bot posts logs to

categories.label: Categories (one per line)
categories.help: settings, admin, user, automated, reports, other

overview: Persistent log of bans, mutes, warns, settings changes and reports.
Category filters: settings, admin, user, automated, reports, other.
Link with /setlog <channelId> (group owner) or from the dashboard.
setup: Create a channel, add the bot as administrator, and set its id here.
Run /setlog <channelId> in the group to bind logging.
troubleshooting: Log channels must be channels; groups cannot receive logs.
Removing the bot from the channel silently stops logging.

cleaning.name: Message Cleaning
cleaning.description: Auto-deletes used commands, service messages, and bot action messages.

cleanServiceTypes.label: Service types (one per line)
cleanServiceTypes.help: join, leave, pin, title, photo, videochat, other

overview: Used commands disappear after execution (by class: admin/user/other).
Service messages (joins, pins, title and photo changes) auto-delete per type.
The bot's own group messages can self-destruct after five minutes.
setup: Enable the module and pick which command classes to clean.
Add service types like join and leave to keep the chat tidy.
troubleshooting: Commands are removed with a short delay so they still execute.
Bot-message cleanup needs no extra rights beyond sending.

topics.name: Forum Topic Management
topics.description: Create, rename, close and delete forum topics from chat commands.

actionTopicId.label: Action topic id (0 = general)
actionTopicId.help: Bot messages route to this forum topic

overview: Forum topic commands: /newtopic, /renametopic, /closetopic, /reopentopic, /deletetopic.
/setactiontopic routes bot output to one topic.
Every command runs inside the topic it affects.
setup: Enable the module in a forum-enabled supergroup.
Grant the bot the manage-topics administrator right.
troubleshooting: These commands only work in forum topics.
Deleting a topic removes its messages permanently.

federation.name: Ban Federations
federation.description: Shared ban lists enforced across all joined chats of every studio bot.

fedNotif.label: Notify the fed owner on actions

overview: One ban list, every group: /fban removes users from all chats in the federation.
Works across every bot in the studio, not just one.
Fed admins, subscriptions (max 5), logs, and CSV/JSON imports.
setup: Create a federation with /newfed <name> in the bot's PM.
Join groups with /joinfed <fedId> (group owner runs it).
Manage bans and imports from the manager below.
troubleshooting: Passive enforcement needs the chat_member update (already enabled).
/leavefed keeps past bans in place until unbanned.

language.name: Bot Reply Language
language.description: Per-group bot reply language (/setlang) for moderation and system messages.

overview: /setlang switches every bot reply between supported languages.
All moderation, captcha, federation and tool messages localize.
User-configured templates (welcome text, notes) stay as written.
setup: Enable the module and pick a default.
Groups change it any time with /setlang.
troubleshooting: Supported languages: English, Turkish, German, Russian, Spanish, Azerbaijani, Arabic, French, Italian, Portuguese, Ukrainian, Persian, Indonesian, Uzbek.
Private chats default to English.

bot2bot.name: Bot-to-Bot Commands
bot2bot.description: Let other bots use this bot's group commands with an admin review gate.

mode.label: Mode
mode.help: off ignores bots, admin trusts admin-bots only, all allows every bot

skipReview.label: Skip the review queue
skipReview.help: Trusted bots act immediately without Approve/Deny buttons

overview: Automation and AI bots can drive moderation commands.
Bot-issued admin actions queue behind inline Approve/Deny buttons.
Skip reviews for trusted bots while keeping their real permissions.
setup: Enable the module and choose a mode (off by default).
Have the other bot send commands like /ban as a normal admin would.
troubleshooting: The acting bot still needs its own Telegram admin rights.
Reviews live in memory and are dropped on restart.
